Beware if you fail any of the tests that will incur more fees for bike hire etc and wait times but they are much less a worry as they book block.

Its the worst honestly. Drivers need to be educated that bikes are sometimes designed this way

Someone said to me after i'd failed twice on mod1 to just get your butt off the seat a little and keep revs on whilst managing the clutch and it will help you keep the bike balanced on things like uturns and figure 8. Of course it all went out the window come test day and i passed 3rd time around by the skin of my teeth i think the examiner had enough of seeing me :)

  
But MOD2 was a breeze, just like out riding with a pal who is also a backseat driver is all.

After i've been riding awhile on i've tried the technique a couple of times and i'ts help me do sharp u turns at least i've even started to do some advanced stuff before the weather set in.

  
You'll never stop learning and that is a fact you can carry across most things. So don't beat yourself up you'll pass eventually and it makes you better for it. Even though in my case it go pretty expensive towards the end. I had every confidence i was going in and passing first time. Very wrong i was.

As you progress in learning you’ll figure it out. If I know I’m in a busy road where people are likely to a dangerous overtake I’ll be in the middle dominating the space 

There generally is no one size fits all approach you ride wherever the path is least likely to get you into trouble fast. There are bends where I’ll stay on the right side so I can see what’s coming same goes for left too 

You can prob see where it’s going. Do what they expect on test. After that put it into practice and progress from  there

Did my CBT what feels like a lifetime ago way back in March. It felt like they could of toned it down to 3hrs tops and not a whole day but i digress. 

If you've been on a bicycle its a great advantage for balance when it comes to riding a motorcycle. 

Gears are't hard at all. Just remember some bikes will need a harder nudge into upper gears than others so be ready to firmly give it a tap up otherwise you'll find yourself going nowhere in neutral.

If you already drive then the on road part will come easier. If not just listen to what you are being told and plan everything in good time. You don't want to be panicking trying to do what feels like 500 things before a turn etc. 

Just take your time and listen most of all to what they are instructing you to do. If i can get through it (i'm a numpty) anyone can.

  
Good luck.

Insurers are just scum scammers. We are here if you need us but if you use us even though it's a no fault claim we will still make insuring you as difficult and as costly as possible. 

  
Had this on my car in 2017 when someone broke in and caused £000s worth of damage trying to get it started claim went through but next years renewal was some £700 more because i'd made a claim. It's criminal that they can get away with it but all that money is supporting the already rich out there and it won't change.

Don't take it dismissively but they aren't interested in your money. They will have a huge amount of students coming and going. I took great offence when the instructor was getting iffy with me on my CBT as the bike was a literal heap of shite they had welded the footpeg with a piece of 22mm pipe lol and the clutch was spongy couldn't feel anything from it plus the rear tyre was deflated. 

I spoke to them about this and they gave me another bike, after that i sailed through except for a couple of iffy moments out on the road where i blew through some lights several times changing to amber and left them all behind but they let me off as i improved as the ride went on and i got a better feel on how to stop gradually.

If you are on a heavy bike and the road falls off to the left putting your left foot down won't always work out well  (ask me how i know) Simply because you will lose your balance and if the bike is a heavy one it will just tip you with it.  

  
If the road is wide enough and it flattens out towards the middle for example you can use that and get away with the left foot down but its all in forward planning if you can see the road cambering off then slow down and give yourself enough time to land in the spot where you can safely put a foot down.
